newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO View - Market jitters cool demand for HK IPOs.
newsitem.headline: IPO View - Market jitters cool demand for HK IPOs.

text.p: Nervousness in the Hong Kong stock market is cooling the fever for initial public offerings (IPOs), especially by China-backed firms, but sentiment should improve in the longer term, analysts said.
The stock market fell significantly over the past week despite predictions that positive sentiment over Britain's return of Hong Kong to China in two weeks would keep pushing stocks higher.

The blue-chip Hang Seng Index fell 542.58 points or 3.7 percent in the week ending Friday to 14,112.55 and the Hang Seng China Enterprises H-shares index, which tracks Chinese enterprises listed in Hong Kong, was down 64.84 points or 6.14 percent to 990.72.
"The coming IPOs response will not be as hot as before as are likely to be dampened by the recent market weakness," said Percy Au-young, director of research at DBS Securities.
Actions by mainland Chinese regulators have dampened investor sentiment and discouraged speculative activity, analysts said.
Beijing recently announced a series of measures, including a ban on state banks investing in stock markets, aimed at calming china's exuberant bourses.
"The correction in the last few days was quite healthy. It has also taught those punters a lesson," said Ann Shih, head of China Research at Kleinwort Benson Securities.

Raymond Jook, a director at SocGen Crosby Securities, agreed that the market weakness would affect IPOs. Companies involved in infrastructure or toll road projects would be affected most because many similar stocks are already listed, he added.
Some analysts said the picture for China-backed IPOs, known as red chips, should brighten in the medium and long term.
"I think the demand will remain strong because right now the market is still short of supply," Shih said.
"However, I do think investors should really be more skeptical and critical because there will be more and more (red-chip IPOs) to come," Shih said.
Hugo So, an analyst at Yamaichi International, said: "The recent weakness is just a mild correction and the overall sentiment is still strong."

Among the H-share IPOs, First Tractor Co Ltd is offering 300 million shares in a global flotation at HK$4.50 per share. Its Hong Kong public offering will close on Monday and dealing in the company's shares is expected to begin on June 23.
Jiangsu Expressway Co Ltd is expected to issue 1.22 billion shares at HK$3.11 each. Its IPO is expected to run from June 18 to 23 with trading beginning on June 27.

Beijing Yanhua Petrochemical Co Ltd is expected to issue 1.012 billion shares at a price ranging from HK$1.77 to HK$2.27 per share. The subscription is expected to run from June 17 to 20 with dealing commencing on June 25.
Toll road operator Greater Beijing Region Expressways Ltd is expected to seek a listing in the third quarter as a red chip.
Analysts said the disappointing trading debut of Jiangxi Copper Co Ltd might also dampen investor sentiment in H-share IPOs in the near term.
Jiangxi Copper shares ended Friday at HK$2.325, against their issue price of HK$2.55.
"Natural resources and petrochemical-related stocks are not that favourable in Hong Kong because investors ... know very little about the businesses," So said.
Hong Kong companies planning to list in the near future include Leading Spirit Conrowa Electric Co Ltd, a unit of Leading Spirit (Holdings) Co Ltd, Fairform Holdings Ltd, and OLS Group Ltd.
